title: Words That Join Ideas
objectives: I can use eight small words to join two ideas.
I can tell what a joining word shows: time, a choice, or a change.
I can read and say sentences with while, until, unless, and although.
I can write a longer sentence by joining two short ones.
rationale: These small words are hard for many learners because they have no picture. They show how one idea relates to another, and they are the first step from short sentences to connected writing. The eight words split into time (while, until), a condition (unless), a surprise or change (although, however, instead, except), and adding (also). Children practice by joining two short sentences, which they can do orally before they write.

words.def: At the same time as something else.
words.ex: Dad cooked dinner while we set the table.
words.ex2: Please stay quiet while the baby is sleeping.

apps.academic: Draw a line to show two actions that happen while one another.
apps.spoken: I can hop while I count to ten.
apps.writing: Use while to show two things that happen at the same time.

cloze.s: I wash the dishes ___ my sister dries them, so we finish together.

cloze2.s: Keep your eyes on the road ___ you ride, so you stay safe.

misuse.s: Tom was asleep while he was running a race.
misuse.why: While means at the same time, and a person cannot be asleep and racing at once.

visual.alt: Two arrows running side by side to show two actions at the same time.

words.def: Up to the time when something happens.
words.ex: We played outside until the sun went down.
words.ex2: Wait here until the bus comes.

apps.academic: Stir the mixture until it is smooth.
apps.spoken: I will wait until you finish.
apps.writing: Use until to show when an action stops.

cloze.s: Please keep stirring ___ the butter melts completely.

cloze2.s: The puppy barked ___ someone opened the door.

misuse.s: The water will keep boiling until it begins to boil.
misuse.why: Until names the end of an action, so the action cannot end when it begins.

visual.alt: An arrow that runs along a line and stops at a flag.

words.ex: We will have a picnic unless it rains.
words.ex2: Do not open the door unless you know who is there.
words.rel: words that add an idea or give a condition

apps.academic: Plants will not grow unless they get water.
apps.spoken: We will play outside unless it storms.
apps.writing: Use unless to name the one thing that would stop a plan.

cloze.s: We will play outside ___ it rains, and then we will stay in and read.

cloze2.s: You cannot go to the park ___ you finish your chores first.

misuse.s: We will go on the picnic unless it is sunny, so we hope for sunshine.
misuse.why: Unless names what would stop the plan, so sunshine would not stop a picnic.

visual.alt: A sunny path and a rainy path with a sign for the only case when the plan changes.

words.ex: Although it was cold, we played outside.
words.ex2: Mia ate her soup although she did not like onions.
words.rel: words that show a different idea

apps.academic: Although the story is short, it has a big lesson.
apps.spoken: Although I was tired, I kept reading.
apps.writing: Use although to show that something is surprising or different.

cloze.s: ___ it was raining hard, the team kept playing soccer.

cloze2.s: Ben smiled ___ he was feeling a little nervous.

misuse.s: Although I was hungry, I ate a big lunch.
misuse.why: Although shows a surprise, but eating when hungry is not surprising, so a word like because fits.

visual.alt: A smiling sun above a child in a raincoat to show two ideas that do not match.

words.def: But; used to show a different idea.
words.ex: The road was long. However, the trip was fun.
words.ex2: I like apples. However, I like oranges even more.
words.rel: words that show a different idea

apps.academic: Writers use however to start a new idea that is different.
apps.spoken: I wanted a pet. However, my building does not allow one.
apps.writing: Use however at the start of a sentence to show a different idea.

cloze.s: The shirt was too big. ___, I wore it with a belt.

cloze2.s: Ana wanted a dog. ___, her building did not allow pets.

misuse.s: I like soccer. However, I like soccer a lot.
misuse.why: However shows a different idea, but this sentence repeats the same idea.

visual.alt: Two arrows pointing in different directions to show two different ideas.

words.ex: We ate fruit instead of cake.
words.ex2: It was too cold to swim, so we skated instead.
words.rel: words that show a different idea

apps.academic: Use a pencil instead of a pen for this page.
apps.writing: Use instead to show one choice that replaces another.

cloze.s: I did not want milk, so I drank juice ___.

cloze2.s: We stayed inside and played games ___ of going to the park in the rain.

misuse.s: Mia drank water instead of water.
misuse.why: Instead means in place of something else, so water cannot replace water.

visual.alt: A glass of juice swapped in place of a glass of milk.

words.ex: Sam likes soccer and also likes swimming.
words.ex2: The zoo has lions, and it also has zebras.
words.rel: words that add an idea or give a condition

apps.writing: Use also to add one more idea that goes with the first.

cloze.s: We saw monkeys at the zoo, and we ___ saw a tall giraffe.

cloze2.s: Dad packed sandwiches, and he ___ packed apples and cheese.

misuse.s: I do not like peas, and I also like peas.
misuse.why: Also adds an idea that fits with the first one, but these two ideas disagree.

visual.alt: A circle with a second circle joined to it to show adding one more idea.

words.frame: I like ___ and I also like ___.

words.ex: Everyone came to the party except Tom.
words.ex2: All the doors are open except the red one.
words.rel: words that show a different idea

apps.academic: Every animal on the list is a mammal except the frog.
apps.spoken: We cleaned every room except the kitchen.
apps.writing: Use except to leave one thing out of a group.

cloze.s: All the kids were in line ___ Mia, who was still tying her shoes.

cloze2.s: We eat every kind of fruit ___ pears, which make Dad sneeze.

misuse.s: Everyone went to the park except everyone.
misuse.why: Except leaves someone out, so everyone cannot be left out.

visual.alt: A row of blue circles with one red circle set apart.

passage.title: A Gray Day at the Park
paras: Tia wanted to go to the park; however, the sky was gray. Dad said, "We will go unless it rains," so Tia drew a kite while they waited.

The rain stopped, so they went, and Tia carried her kite instead of a ball. Although the wind was soft, the kite flew high, and a butterfly also floated by. They stayed until sunset, and everyone left except the ducks.

qs.q: What does "unless" mean in "We will go unless it rains"?
choices: We will go only if it rains.
We will go if it does not rain.
qs.why: Unless means if not, so they will go when there is no rain.

qs.q: What did Tia carry instead of a ball?
qs.why: The story says Tia carried her kite instead of a ball.

qs.q: Who was still at the park at sunset?
qs.why: Everyone left except the ducks, so the ducks stayed.

write.prompt: Write or tell what you will do this weekend. Use unless or while.
write.frame: I will ___ unless ___. I will ___ while ___.

study.task: Sort the eight words into three groups: time words, different-idea words, and add-or-choose words. Then pick one word and join two short sentences with it.

groups.label: words that show a different idea
words that add an idea or give a condition

sentences: Write a sentence about two things you do at the same time. Use while.
Write a sentence that tells how long you keep doing something. Use until.
Write a sentence about a plan that could change. Use unless.

combine.model: Although it was raining, we played outside.
Lena likes pizza, and she also likes salad.

discuss: Which joining word helps you tell about two things at once? Which helps you leave something out?
How is although different from because?
produce.explain: Explain how however is different from also. Use both words in your answer.

argue.prompt: Is it better to play outside or read inside? Pick one and use instead in your reason.
argue.frame: I would rather ___ instead of ___ because ___.

constructed.prompt: Tell what you do after school. Use while and until.
look: tells two actions at once with while
tells when something stops with until
constructed.model: I do my homework while my brother reads. I keep working until I finish.

constructed.prompt: Write about a day at school. Use although and except.
look: shows a surprise or difference with although
leaves one thing out with except
constructed.model: Although the test was hard, I tried my best. I knew every answer except the last one.

teacher.overview: Children learn eight small words that connect ideas: time (while, until), a condition (unless), a change or surprise (although, however, instead, except), and adding (also). These words have no pictures, so use movement, line diagrams, and two-sentence joining. Practice orally before writing.

notes.va.while.conj: Act out two actions at the same time: pat your head while rubbing your tummy. Contrast with first, next, then. Spanish speakers: mientras.
notes.va.until.conj: Use a movement that stops at a signal: Hop until I clap. Link to time words from grade 1 such as before and after.
notes.va.unless.conj: Unless means if not. Practice with rule sentences: We go outside unless it rains. Children often confuse unless with until because the words look alike.
notes.va.although.conj: Show a surprise: It was raining, but we played. Although it was raining, we played. Start with although at the front, then try it in the middle. Even though is an easy synonym to say.
notes.va.however.adv: However usually starts a new sentence and follows a period. Contrast with and (adds) and but (changes) so children hear the difference.
notes.va.instead.adv: Use a swap with real objects: a pen instead of a pencil. The words instead of need an object; instead alone ends the sentence.
notes.va.also.adv: Also adds a new idea. Practice with two facts about an animal. The word too is a synonym that goes at the end of a sentence.
notes.va.except.prep: Show a group and take one away: all the pencils except the red one. Except is easy to confuse with accept; use only except.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'I read: We will have a picnic unless it rains. Unless means if not. So we will have the picnic if it does not rain. If it rains, no picnic.'
discuss: Which word tells you something is different or surprising?
How can a joining word make two short sentences into one?
misconceptions: Children may mix up unless and until. Unless names a stopper; until names a time.
Some children use however in the middle of a sentence without a comma or period. Model it at the start of a new sentence.
Children may think instead and also mean the same. Instead swaps; also adds.
extend: Write two short sentences on cards and have children glue them together with a joining word.
Find joining words in a read-aloud and put a sticky note on each.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit suggest, disappointed, and wave: a child might suggest a plan unless it rains and feel disappointed when it does; a friend might wave while saying goodbye.

wida.oral: Say two short sentences. Your partner joins them with a joining word and says the new sentence.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (mientras, hasta que, a menos que, aunque, sin embargo, en lugar de, también, excepto) not reviewed by a native speaker; function words have several correct Spanish forms.
Visual diagrams for function words use the contrast, flow, and web types; the UI composes them from the alt descriptions.
